about: Review #471 A1 (lab PR 267): a program staged in /tmp listens on port 8080, then executes /usr/sbin/nginx in the same pid (the socket is inherited). In kernel order the listener is judged on the staged program; on the priority bus the exec (P1) is taken ahead of the listener (P3) and NN-L-NET-006/019's installed-service exemption read nginx; judged as of the listener's time it is the staged program's.

switches.held: the kill of the shell's process tree (R020, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the scan kill threshold (NN-L-NET-026, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the brute-force kill threshold (NN-L-NET-027, lab PR 224)
the kill for a flow to port 53 of a server that is no configured resolver (port 53 was exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of an allowlisted transfer tool whose lineage holds a precursor (exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of the ransomware actor's process tree (NN-L-IMP-001, lab PR 225)
the kill of the staged program that asked a security tool off (NN-L-EVA, lab PR 225)
the kill for a rename seen only as a watched directory's new entry (NN-L-FIM-010, a match added by lab PR 225)

decision.name: Exec from /tmp/
decision.reasoning: Process executed from /tmp/ — common malware staging location

decision.name: Wildcard-bind listener on uncommon port
decision.reasoning: New listener bound to the wildcard address on port 8080, a common service port, from a program not installed in a root-owned system tree (its executable, or the script an interpreter runs, lies elsewhere or cannot be read) from a non-allowlisted comm — network-exposed backdoor surface (T1571); posture → ALERTED [also matched: NN-L-NET-006_UncommonListener (Log, Medium)]
